banners.name: gyropup
banners.title: Gyropup
banners.tagline: A research robot designed to balance on two wheel-legs, with a foam-ball turret: CAD and simulation in the open.
banners.desc: What is designed now, set as in docs/hero.jpg: the bench stand is traced, the foam-ball turret drops onto it on its compute plinth, leg v2 (the five-bar on two RS-04s, two links meeting at the wheel) slides in beside it, then the turret head scans left and right about its pan axis, nods about its tilt axis and holds a lock-on. Built by the project's own CadQuery code (cad/build_leg.py, cad/turret.py, cad/turret_stand.py) with hidden lines removed.

banners.name: val-ark
banners.tagline: An offline-first mirror that fills a disk with open-source tools, AI models and Wikipedia, then serves it over local wifi.
banners.desc: A disk fills cell by cell from Val Ark's real catalogue (its 50 tool scripts, its extra-model table and its installer table), one of each kind first, as the Librarian plans it; then wifi arcs pulse as it serves the mirror to the local network.

banners.name: j501-agx-orin
banners.tagline: A 3D-printable enclosure for the Seeed reServer J501 carrier and an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin.
banners.desc: The Rev 0.9 enclosure drawn from its real STEP files with hidden lines removed: the base is traced, the rear plate and front plate slide down into their channels, the side hatch slides in and the cover drops on.

banners.name: logitech_bcc950
banners.tagline: A talking eyeball on a stick: pan, tilt and zoom control for the Logitech BCC950 on Linux.

motif.source: src/python/bcc950/constants.py: ZOOM_MIN 100, ZOOM_MAX 500, pan and tilt speed -1..1

banners.desc: The BCC950 drawn as an eyeball on a stick: it pans and tilts around, its pupil zooms over the camera's 100 to 500 range, it blinks, and a speech bubble of level bars talks.

banners.name: pcb-agx-thor-can-breakout
banners.title: Thor CAN breakout
banners.tagline: Protected CAN breakout boards and printed housings for NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor, in KiCad and CadQuery.
banners.desc: The two-port board drawn from its KiCad layout: the outline is traced, pads and copper settle, the J47 header and both DE9 ports drop on, the CAN0 and CAN1 pairs are laid from the header to their ports, and pulses run along each pair, high and low in step.

banners.name: graphdone

banners.tagline: Relationship management for agents. People and AI agents coordinate through dependencies and outcomes.

items: Carry ports and buses into item wiring
motif.source: GraphDone-Core's open issues: dynamic level of detail (#193) with its wiring (#220) and MCP authoring (#217) steps, topology organization (#233), exact-SHA releases (#190) and the installer fix (#243). The issues are unassigned: the person and AI-agent owners are illustrative, as GraphDone work is owned by either

banners.desc: GraphDone's current work as a live topology: work items from its open issues ride an orbit round their outcome, drawn as GraphDone's logo, each a node in its type's colour with an illustrative owner (a person or an AI agent) and named by a HUD callout with its issue number, over a perspective grid and drifting layers of distant graph. The items complete in dependency order: each node fills, its dependency arcs and its neon spoke to the outcome light and data pulses flow inward, and one of the logo's work nodes comes on; when every item is done the outcome locks and the readout reads 6/6 done.

banners.alt: GraphDone: one graph of work for people and AI agents. The open-source core (web app, GraphQL API, MCP server), the hosted app at graphdone.com, AI agents and people connect round shared outcomes.
banners.desc: GraphDone as one system: the open-source core's web app, GraphQL API and MCP server, the hosted app at graphdone.com built on that core, and the AI agents and people who work in the same graph ride an orbit round GraphDone's logo, each named by a HUD callout, over a perspective grid and drifting layers of distant graph.
